meta.title: Cove Studio — a coding platform that started in a real classroom
meta.description: From a student running their first line of code to a teacher running the room, Cove Studio holds the whole lesson. Python in the browser, automatic grading, live class monitoring.

hero.title: The coding environment a class actually runs on
hero.lead: No twenty minutes lost to install instructions. Students open a browser and start writing; teachers see how far the whole room has gotten on one screen.

student.title: Nobody gets left stuck
student.lead: The problem, the editor, and the output share one screen. Submitting shows which test failed and why, and a hint opens right where it was asked for.
student.point_1_body: It runs inside the browser, so a school laptop and an academy desktop behave the same way.
student.point_2_body: Exercises using input() run for real in a terminal, prompt and answer both.
student.point_3_body: Which input, what was expected, what came back instead.
student.point_4_body: The answer is never handed over first. A student asks, and it opens in place.
student.shot_alt: The student view — problem description, code editor, and result panel

teacher.title: You can see what's happening in the room
teacher.lead: Finding out who's stuck shouldn't mean walking a lap. It's on the roster, and if you need to, you can open that student's screen.
teacher.point_1_body: Who's connected and how far along, per student, as it changes.
teacher.point_2_body: Their code and their output, live, down to where the cursor is.
teacher.point_3_body: Build the curriculum, assign it to a class, enrol the students — in one place.
teacher.point_4_body: Description, starter code, test cases, and hints, authored by the teacher.
teacher.shot_alt: The teacher monitoring view — class roster with live progress

flow.title: Curriculum to evidence, without a gap
flow.step_1_body: Design the course as subjects, chapters, and lessons.
flow.step_2_body: Enrol students and assign the teacher who takes them.
flow.step_3_body: Students solve; teachers watch the same screen.
flow.step_4_body: Submissions and results accumulate into a reason for what comes next.

detail.title: The things that used to get in the way
detail.item_1_body: The whole interface is ready in both.
detail.item_2_body: Whichever a student picks, it's remembered.
detail.item_3_body: Chrome, Edge, Safari, and Firefox all behave the same.
detail.item_4_body: Members and permissions are scoped to the institution they belong to.

close.title: Thinking about bringing it in?
close.lead: An academy, a school, or a university can start with a single class. Tell us how you teach and we'll propose the setup that fits.
